quiz.0.question: In what year was the DOCG system established?
quiz.0.explanation: The DOCG (Denominazione di Origine Controllata e Garantita) system was officially established by Decree in 1980, with Brunello di Montalcino, Barolo, Barbaresco, Vino Nobile di Montepulciano and Chianti among the first wines designated.
quiz.1.question: What is the most significant difference between DOCG and DOC?
quiz.1.options.0: DOCG wines are always more expensive
quiz.1.options.1: DOCG requires official government tasting panels to approve every batch before release; DOC does not
quiz.1.options.2: DOCG allows more grape varieties in the blend
quiz.1.options.3: DOC wines can be exported; DOCG cannot
quiz.1.explanation: The key difference: all DOCG wines must pass a government-appointed tasting commission (commissione di degustazione) before they can be released — adding a layer of quality control absent from DOC.
quiz.2.question: What unique physical feature must appear on a DOCG wine label?
quiz.2.options.1: A numbered government seal (fascia) across the bottle neck/cap
quiz.2.options.2: A QR code linking to the producer's website
quiz.2.explanation: Every DOCG bottle must carry a numbered government seal (fascia or contrassegno) affixed across the cap or cork — guaranteeing the wine has passed inspection. Each seal is unique and traceable.
quiz.3.question: As of 2024, how many DOCGs does Italy have?
quiz.3.explanation: As of 2024, Italy has 77 DOCGs and 341 DOCs — the most complex appellation system of any wine-producing country, reflecting Italy's extraordinary diversity of regions and grape varieties.
